parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the volume of the shed.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the length of a sloping edge of the roof, from the top of a wall to the ridge.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the angle that a sloping edge of the roof, from part (b), makes with the horizontal.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Find the total area of the two sloping faces of the roof.

parts.label: e
parts.text: Roofing felt is sold in rolls that each cover 4 m\(^{2}\). Find the number of rolls needed for the roof.

parts.label: f
parts.text: Find the length of the longest straight rod that fits inside the cuboid part of the shed.

parts.label: g
parts.text: Find the angle between this rod and the floor.

parts.label: h
parts.text: The outside walls of the shed, including the two triangular ends of the roof, are to be painted. Find the area to be painted.

idea: The shed is a cuboid plus a prism whose cross-section is a triangle with base 2 m and height 0.8 m. Lengths and angles in 3D come from right-angled triangles: find one in the right plane, then use Pythagoras or trigonometry.

solution.label: a
steps: Cuboid: \(3 \times 2 \times 2 = 12\). Roof: triangle \(\dfrac{1}{2} \times 2 \times 0.8 = 0.8\), times the length 3: \(2.4\).

solution.label: b
steps: Half the width is 1 m and the rise is 0.8 m: \(\sqrt{1^{2} + 0.8^{2}} = \sqrt{1.64} = 1.280\ldots\)

solution.label: e
steps: \(7.68\ldots \div 4 = 1.92\ldots\), so one roll is not enough.

solution.label: f
steps: The space diagonal of the cuboid: \(\sqrt{3^{2} + 2^{2} + 2^{2}} = \sqrt{17} = 4.123\ldots\)

solution.label: g
steps: The diagonal of the floor is \(\sqrt{3^{2} + 2^{2}} = \sqrt{13}\), and the rod rises 2 m above it.

stem: A car's windscreen wiper arm is 60 cm long and turns about a pivot through an angle of \(110^\circ\). The rubber blade lies along the arm, from 15 cm to 60 cm from the pivot.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the length of the arc traced by the tip of the wiper in one sweep.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the area of windscreen cleaned by the blade in one sweep.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find this area as a percentage of the area of the sector of radius 60 cm with angle \(110^\circ\).

parts.label: d
parts.text: Find the straight-line distance between the positions of the tip at the two ends of a sweep.

parts.label: e
parts.text: Find the area between this straight line and the arc traced by the tip.

parts.label: f
parts.text: The wiper makes 45 sweeps out and 45 sweeps back each minute. Find the mean speed of the tip, in cm per second.

idea: An arc with angle \(\theta\) in a circle of radius \(r\) has length \(\dfrac{\theta}{360} \times 2\pi r\), and a sector has area \(\dfrac{\theta}{360} \times \pi r^{2}\). The cleaned area is a large sector minus a small one. A segment is a sector minus a triangle.

solution.label: d
steps: The two radii and the line form an isosceles triangle. Cosine rule: \(\sqrt{60^{2} + 60^{2} - 2 \times 60 \times 60 \cos 110^\circ} = 98.29\ldots\)

solution.label: f
steps: In one minute the tip travels \(90 \times 115.1\ldots = 10\,367.2\ldots\) cm.

stem: Three villages are joined by straight roads. Village Q is 8.4 km from village P on a bearing of \(065^\circ\). Village R is 6.1 km from P on a bearing of \(140^\circ\).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that angle QPR is \(75^\circ\).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the distance QR.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the area of the triangle PQR.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Find the angle PQR.

parts.label: e
parts.text: Find the bearing of R from Q.

parts.label: f
parts.text: Find the shortest distance from P to the road QR. Use your unrounded answers to parts (b) and (c).

parts.label: g
parts.text: A cyclist rides from Q to R at 18 km per hour. Find the time taken, to the nearest minute.

idea: Bearings are measured clockwise from north, so the angle between two bearings from the same point is their difference. The shortest distance from a point to a line is along the perpendicular; it can be found from the area of the triangle.

solution.label: a
steps: Both bearings are measured from P: \(140^\circ - 65^\circ\).

solution.label: d
steps: Sine rule: \(\sin \mathrm{PQR} = \dfrac{6.1 \sin 75^\circ}{9.013\ldots}\), so \(\angle \mathrm{PQR} = 40.82\ldots^\circ\) (acute, because it is opposite the shortest side).

solution.label: e
steps: The bearing of P from Q is \(065^\circ + 180^\circ = 245^\circ\).
R is on the other side of QP from the north line, so turn anticlockwise from QP by angle PQR: \(245^\circ - 40.82\ldots^\circ = 204.1\ldots^\circ\)

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write down the equation of the perpendicular bisector of AB.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the equation of the perpendicular bisector of AC. Give your answer in the form \(y = mx + c\).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the coordinates of the point V that is the same distance from A, B and C.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Show that V is further from D than from A, so that V is a vertex of the Voronoi diagram.

parts.label: e
parts.text: A visitor is at the point \((4, 5)\). Determine which truck the visitor goes to.

parts.label: f
parts.text: A fifth truck is to be parked as far as possible from A, B and C, at V. Find its distance from each of them, in metres.

parts.label: g
parts.text: Explain why trucks A, B and C all lose part of their cells when the fifth truck arrives.

idea: A point on the perpendicular bisector of two sites is the same distance from both. Where the bisectors of AB and AC meet is equidistant from A, B and C; it is a vertex of the Voronoi diagram if no other site is nearer.

solution.label: a
steps: A and B have the same \(y\)-coordinate, and the midpoint of AB is \((5, 2)\).

solution.label: b
steps: Midpoint of AC: \((3.5, 5)\). Gradient of AC: \(\dfrac{8 - 2}{5 - 2} = 2\), so the perpendicular gradient is \(-\dfrac{1}{2}\).

solution.label: d
steps: \(6.209\ldots > 3.75\), so no site is nearer to V than A, B and C.

solution.label: f
steps: \(\mathrm{VA} = \mathrm{VB} = \mathrm{VC} = 3.75\) units, and each unit is 10 m.

solution.label: g
steps: Points just round V are now nearer the new truck than A, B or C, and V touches the cells of all three.
solution.answer: V is on the boundary of all three of their cells, so the new cell round V takes a piece of each

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the height of the mast.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the angle of elevation of T from Q.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the distance PQ.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Find the lengths of the two cables.

parts.label: e
parts.text: Find the angle PTQ between the two cables.

parts.label: f
parts.text: Find the area of the triangle PTQ.

idea: Use the right-angled triangles BPT, BQT and BPQ, each in its own plane. Triangle PTQ is not right-angled, so use the cosine rule with its three sides.

stem: A swimming pool is 25 m long and 10 m wide. The depth of the water when the pool is full is 1.2 m at the shallow end and 2.8 m at the deep end, and the floor slopes in a straight line between them, as shown in the side view.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the volume of the pool.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The pool is filled at 40 m\(^{3}\) per hour. Find the time taken to fill it.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the length of the sloping floor.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Find the angle between the floor and the horizontal.

parts.label: e
parts.text: The floor and the four walls are tiled. Find the area to be tiled.

parts.label: f
parts.text: For a competition, the water is kept 0.2 m below the full level. Find the volume of water in the pool then, and the percentage of the full volume this is.

idea: The pool is a prism: its cross-section is the trapezium in the side view, and it is 10 m wide. The two long walls are trapezia, the end walls rectangles, and the floor a rectangle whose length is the sloping edge.
